answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make trust accrue from costly, verifiable work rather than from a mere name. New identities start with tight rate limits and must complete attested, useful tasks over time before they gain larger transaction rights, so spawning thousands of fakes buys no instant influence. Like a lagoon that admits water only through a narrow channel, or an orchard where each tree must be planted and tended before it bears fruit, reputation should grow slowly from proven behavior, not from signing a new identity into existence with a quill stroke.
